IN: how MongoDB Retryable Writes began and changed over time, covering the driver-spec contract, the server-side mechanism, the version milestones, and the primary sources for each. OUT: sibling and adjacent concepts. These are Retryable Reads, Driver Sessions, Causal Consistency, multi-document Transactions, CSOT, and Client Backpressure. Each is a separate frontier item. This report mentions them only where a retryable-writes claim depends on them.

In scope: the retryable-writes contract between MongoDB drivers and servers. That covers when a write can be retried, how the retry runs, and where the at-most-once guarantee breaks down. Out of scope: retryable reads, multi-document transactions as a feature, sessions and causal consistency in general, CSOT design, and sharding internals beyond their effect on retry correctness. Each of these is a separate frontier item.
